title: harness: codex-pace-guard (Codex over weekly threshold)
desc: Blocks codex exec when Codex token usage exceeds the weekly threshold. Redirects to Haiku or waits for reset.
steps: SAFETY: Fires when Codex weekly token usage exceeds the configured block threshold (read from codex_measured_limit.json, default 3M tokens). Prevents runaway Codex spend when the budget is exhausted.
SOLUTION: switch to --model haiku for the immediate task, OR wait for the weekly reset (Thursday 18:00 KST). Haiku covers most read/survey/search tasks Codex handles.

PREVENTION: monitor Codex pace via wkdoctor (per-family pace dashboard). At ~80 percent of the weekly budget switch non-critical tasks to Haiku; the 95 percent circuit breaker speaks an alert before the hard block.

CURRENT STATE + KNOWN BUG (2026-06-29): the weekly percent can read GARBAGE (e.g. 344 percent, limit=2M) because codex_balance.json source=sqlite-auto carries USED tokens only -- no remainingPct and no limit -- so the hardcoded 2M fallback overflows. The data-driven fix (dynLimitM back-calc + anomaly-triggered CLI re-scrape via the wkstdpty /status writer + the display-honesty UNVERIFIED diff) lives in harness-codex-pace-guard-howto; the dated root-cause and the live blockers (missing ConPTY .cs, dangling codex.exe symlink) live in harness-codex-pace-guard-ref. Do NOT confabulate a limit number -- use the dashboard remainingPct or the observed faint-point, both real data.

NAVIGATION: build recipes, the dynLimitM formula, the remainingPct-vs-usedPct parsing semantic, and the 7-change display diff -> wkappbot skill read harness-codex-pace-guard-howto. Dated incidents, forensics, and blockers -> wkappbot skill read harness-codex-pace-guard-ref. Both are part of this cluster. Cross: harness-active-model-scoping, guard-feeding-cache-confirm-before-block, wk-tool-sub-1s-response-time-mandate.
